questions.q: What is a trigger in a Power Automate flow?
options: A step that runs after an action completes
The single event that starts the flow
A connector that only works with SharePoint
An optional component that most flows don't need
questions.explain: A trigger is the event that starts a cloud flow — every flow has exactly one, and nothing in the flow runs until it fires.

questions.q: A Castlebridge dock worker wants to flag a damaged pallet on the spot by tapping a button in the mobile app. Which trigger type fits?
options: Scheduled
Automated
Instant
Recurring
questions.explain: Instant triggers fire manually, such as from a button selected in the Power Automate mobile app — exactly the scenario of flagging something on the spot.

questions.q: What is the minimum a Power Automate flow needs before it can be saved?
options: At least three actions and no trigger
One trigger and one action
A condition and a loop
A connection to Microsoft Teams specifically
questions.explain: Power Automate requires at least one trigger and one action before a flow can be saved — everything else is a variation on that minimum shape.

questions.q: In what order do actions in a flow run by default?
options: In random order, determined at runtime
All actions run simultaneously regardless of placement
In the order they're placed, top to bottom, unless branched by a condition or repeated by a loop
In reverse order, bottom to top
questions.explain: Actions execute in the order they're placed in the designer, top to bottom, unless that order is altered by a condition branch or a loop.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an automated trigger?
options: A flow that starts when a new item is created in a SharePoint list
A flow started by tapping a button in the mobile app
A flow that runs every day at 6 AM regardless of events
A flow that only starts when a developer runs it manually from code
questions.explain: An automated trigger fires on an event in a connected service, such as a new item being created in a SharePoint list — no manual action or fixed schedule is involved.
